projects.name: IFAD - 1100001674 - PSA (Pro-Semiarid Project)
projects.description: The Pro-Semiarid: Rural Sustainable Development Project in the Semi-arid Region of Bahia aims to promote rural development based on agroecological principles, with productive inclusion, and generation of employment and income. The construction of water supply systems, agro-industries, technical assistance and rural extension (ATER), technical training for producers and work in socio-productive cooperation networks are among the actions implemented by this project. The project's actions are coordinated regionally by the Territorial Support Services for Family Agriculture (SETAFs): Juazeiro, Senhor do Bonfim and Jacobina. In addition, the project has ten local ATER entities, 25 agronomists, veterinarians and social workers, 115 agricultural technicians and 115 young people, between 19 and 25 years old, who act as Rural Community Agents (ACR), acting directly in 460 communities in 32 selected municipalities, in five Identity Territories. The municipalities covered by the Project are: Capim Grosso, Quixabeira, Várzea do Poço, Caem, Jacobina, Mirangaba, Ourolândia, Saúde, Serrolândia, Umburanas, Várzea Nova, Miguel Calmon, Andorinha, Antônio Gonçalves, Caldeirão Grande, Campo Formoso, Philadelphia, Jaguarari, Pindobaçu, Ponto Novo, Senhor do Bonfim, Itiúba, Queimadas, Casa Nova, Curaçá, Juazeiro, Remanso, Sento Sé, Sobradinho, Uauá, Campo Alegre de Lourdes and Pilão Arcado.

projects.name: FAO GCP/BRA/092P/GFF - Sustaining Healthy Coastal and Marine Ecosystems (PPG)
projects.description:
In line with the Brazilian Blue Initiative, the proposed project seeks to reinforce and expand current efforts to protect and manage Brazil’s extensive coastal and marine environments and the rich biodiversity and ecosystem services they support, fostering an enabling environment for a sustainable and equitable Blue Economy based on this natural capital. More specifically, the project aims at improving the management and financial sustainability of the Marine and Coastal Protected Area (MCPA) system by: (i) strengthening the capacities of key institutions such as the Interministerial Commission for Marine Resources (CIRM); (ii) by strengthening and ensuring long term sustainability of the financing strategy of the MCPA system; and (iii) by enhancing biodiversity monitoring and assessing gaps and needs for effective connectivity across the MCPA system. The project will support the implementation of MCPA management plans in selected target sites and implement actions to address threats to biodiversity in these sites. 

In parallel, the project will support actions to help mainstream Blue Economy principles; and support innovative approaches and technologies for the conservation and sustainable use of marine and coastal resources. Additionally, the project will support local, national and international knowledge exchange and collaboration, helping to build the capacity of Brazilian stakeholders to effectively contribute to the management and sustainable use of coastal and marine environments as the foundation for a Blue Economy.

projects.name: UN WOMEN Human Rights of Indigenous and Quilombola Women: A Governance Matter
projects.description: The project is implemented in the border states of Maranhão and Pará with an expressive presence of both Indigenous and Quilombola communities living in forest areas (North and Northeast regions). UN Women draws on its strong partnerships with Indigenous women’s networks sustained since 2014 through the “Voices of Indigenous Women” group and with Quilombola’s CONAQ to facilitate integration of their rights in governance processes, which directly affects them and their communities’ lives. Prioritizing the Indigenous and Quilombola women, the most marginalized and vulnerable population groups, UN Women implements the SDG Leaving No One Behind principle, which is particularly relevant in the selected two states. The project facilitates inclusion and meaningful participation of these women in policy-making, state and municipal planning and budgeting, thus ensuring that the governance processes in Maranhão and Pará go beyond averages, aim to reach everyone and thus, prevent and eliminate discrimination and inequalities based on gender, race and ethnicity. Taking into account that Indigenous and Quilombola women face higher risks and greater burdens from the impacts of deforestation and climate change, the project also aims to address the compound inequalities and discrimination that often prevent women from fully contributing to climate-related planning, policy-making and implementation.

projects.name: UN WOMEN UNFPA UNHCR Leadership, Empowerment, Access and Protection of Migrant, Asylum-Seeker and Refugee Women in Brazil
projects.description:
The Joint Programme (JP) “Leadership, Empowerment, Access and Protection (LEAP) for migrant, asylum seeker and refugee women in Brazil”, funded by the Government of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, serves as a platform to coordinate efforts of the three participating United Nations Organizations (PUNOs) – United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) and UN Women to promote gender equality and women’s empowerment in the national humanitarian response to the Venezuelan exodus. In humanitarian crises, the most affected populations are women and girls. Poverty, partial or complete family separation, changes gender roles, barriers in access to protection and services and exposure to higher risks of violence have created a situation of increased vulnerability for Venezuelan women in Roraima, especially those living in the streets.
The Joint Programme’s overall objective is to support the Brazilian government in adequately responding to the needs of migrant, asylum seeker, refugee, and host women in Brazil. At the end of the Joint Programme, it is expected that the national response to the mixed influx of Venezuelan nationals in Brazil is more gender inclusive and responsive. The Joint Programme aims to strengthen protection and support mechanisms for migrant, asylum seeker refugee and host women; promote migrant, asylum seeker, refugee and host women’s economic empowerment, opportunities and rights; and promote migrant, asylum seeker, refugee and host women’s empowerment, leadership and substantive participation in the humanitarian response. The Joint Programme builds on comparative advantages of the participating UN Agencies, as well as on complementarity of their mandates and expertise.

projects.name: UN WOMEN Multistakeholders partnerships for a transformative change towards gender equality and women’s empowerment (HeforShe, Unstereotype Alliance and WEPs)
projects.description:
Multistakeholders partnerships for a transformative change towards gender equality and women’s empowerment are established by UN Women Brazil to address stereotypes in marketing and communications (Unstereotype Alliance); to engage men as allies (HeForShe); to ensure the workplace is an enabling environment for women (WEPs). The key objective is to ensure that the private sector recognizes the importance and benefits of gender equality, and actively promotes it within and beyond their circles of influence, resulting in cultural and social change at organizational, community and institutional levels, influencing the public agenda. Mobilizing the private sector, not only as a funding source, but as strategic partners for the promotion of decent work for women, providing concrete measures and targets for reaching gender equality in the workplace.   

The Unstereotype Alliance, a thought and action platform that uses advertising as a force for good to drive positive change. It seeks to eradicate harmful gender-based stereotypes. The alliance is focused on empowering women in all their diversity (race, class, age, ability, ethnicity, religion, sexuality, language, education, etc.) and addressing harmful masculinities to help create a gender equal world. The Alliance brings together a powerful growing global coalition of leading industry players behind the common goal of eliminating gender bias and harmful gender stereotypes from their advertising.

The HeForShe solidarity movement for gender equality, which provides a systematic approach and targeted platform on which men and boys can engage and become change agents towards the achievement of gender equality. Achieving gender equality in our lifetimes requires an innovative, inclusive approach that both recognizes men and boys as partners for women’s rights and acknowledges the ways in which they also benefit from this equality. HeForShe invites men and boys to build on the work of the women’s movement as equal partners, crafting and implementing a shared vision of gender equality that will benefit all of humanity.
The Women’s Empowerment Principles (WEPs) are a set of Principles to which companies and organization commit and which offer guidance to business on how to promote gender equality and women’s empowerment in the workplace, marketplace and community. Established by UN Global Compact and UN Women, the WEPs are informed by international labour and human rights standards and grounded in the recognition that businesses have a stake in, and a responsibility for, gender equality and women’s empowerment.

projects.description:
PrEP Project - Salvador
MAIN GOAL
Encouraging the adherence of transgender women and transvestites to the treatment of HIV Pre Exposure Prophylaxis and expand information on HIV/AIDS, syphilis and viral hepatitis, as well as combination prevention in Municipalities of Salvador and Lauro de Freitas through the implementation of the PrEP Trans Project.

SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES:
a) Train navigators to act in peer education (combined HIV/STI prevention, offer of voluntary testing, support for linking to health services through agents navigators, and support for treatment adherence);
b) Promote HIV counseling, PrEP and emotional support to the beneficiary public for bonding the PrEP programs available in Salvador;
c) Provide support actions in Telemedicine in the social, psychological and health fields for the key project population;
d) Disseminate the combined prevention strategy, with an emphasis on PrEP, through educational materials communication, communication channel and online events.

Bora Saber Project in Boa Vista (RR) and Belém (PA)
OBJECTIVE
Increase the access to HIV testing and ensure the link to health services for ART initiation and retention based on the 90/90/90 Goals.


GOALS
•        Increase the uptake of HIV testing among adolescents and youth 15- 24 by 30% 
•        Linkage of at least 90% of all HIV positive cases diagnosed to health services for treatment initiation

STRATEGY 
HIV testing will be conducting during outreach activities. Youth and adolescents will be visiting hot spots with high concentration of most vulnerable populations such as MSM, transgender, migrants and refugee, to promote peer HIV/AIDS/STI prevention, and offer voluntary HIV testing, counseling and inputs, and combination prevention. The activities performed in a non-health service environment (more community-based), can access these populations better and can deliver healthcare in a way that a formal health care structure cannot. The navigators (peers) will escort the HIV positive cases to health services for immediate ART initiation. Additionally, retention groups will support the adherence to ART. A consultative group will be established to follow up the project, with participation of municipal health representatives, NGOs, youth and adolescent networks, and UNFPA. 


BENEFICIARY POPULATION
Adolescents and youth from key populations including men who have sex with men, transgender, migrants and refugees.  The project will target adolescents and young people in hot spot areas including cruising areas, venues, and migrant and refugee shelters. 

The project will use established platforms to articulate a multi-sectoral response to engage partners from outside the health system. Community links are also key to a successful HIV response, as Brazil clearly demonstrated in the past.  The engagement and participation of youth and adolescents will be key to the success and UNFPA will work with existing networks of young people living with HIV and LGBTI groups to ensure their full involvement in all stages of the project, including their full participation in the coordination mechanism to be established at municipal level.

projects.name: UNFPA Providing oxygen supply to maternity hospitals in Manaus, Brazil
projects.description: The North is one of the most impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic:  87.1% of pregnant and postpartum women who have died of Covid were black. In the Northeast, this number is 71.1%. In the South region, however, it drops to 13.7%.These data reveal the immense challenge for UNFPA, as its global strategy is to achieve the three zeros by 2030: zero unmet need for contraception, zero preventable maternal deaths, and zero violence and harmful practices against women and girls.Thus, the purpose of the project in question – providing for the donation of an oxygen plant to a maternal and child health unit in Manaus – prevents the repetition of the scenario of oxygen shortage in times of high demand, such as that seen in January 2021. The oxygen plant donated to Ana Braga Maternity, located in Manaus, has the capacity to produce 31 cubic meters per hour, which is sufficient to supply, on average, up to 70 beds, which meets 100% of the current demand at the maternity hospital. Undoubtedly, the partnership between the UN Population Fund and the Norwegian Embassy seems essential to encourage projects capable of strengthening support for women and children affected by the pandemic and aggravated by country’s chronic income inequality. We must not forget that maternal death perpetuates the cycle of poverty in society, brings great suffering to families and uncovers the violation of women's rights to their own and their babies’ health. Therefore, to contribute to and support initiatives so that sexual and reproductive rights are guaranteed and essential public services are maintained in full, throughout different sectors and territories, is essential during the Covid-19 pandemic.

projects.description:
The Joint Programme (JP) “Leadership, Empowerment, Access and Protection (LEAP) for migrant, asylum seeker and refugee women in Brazil”, funded by the Government of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, serves as a platform to coordinate efforts of the three participating United Nations Organizations (PUNOs) – United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) and UN Women to promote gender equality and women’s empowerment in the national humanitarian response to the Venezuelan exodus. In humanitarian crises, the most affected populations are women and girls. Poverty, partial or complete family separation, changes gender roles, barriers in access to protection and services and exposure to higher risks of violence have created a situation of increased vulnerability for Venezuelan women in Roraima, especially those living in the streets.
The Joint Programme’s overall objective is to support the Brazilian government in adequately responding to the needs of migrant, asylum seeker, refugee, and host women in Brazil. At the end of the Joint Programme, it is expected that the national response to the mixed influx of Venezuelan nationals in Brazil is more gender inclusive and responsive. The Joint Programme aims to strengthen protection and support mechanisms for migrant, asylum seeker refugee and host women; promote migrant, asylum seeker, refugee and host women’s economic empowerment, opportunities and rights; and promote migrant, asylum seeker, refugee and host women’s empowerment, leadership and substantive participation in the humanitarian response. The Joint Programme builds on comparative advantages of the participating UN Agencies, as well as on complementarity of their mandates and expertise.

The preparatory phase includes the following results: 1. Assessment of the Camaragibe landfill and recommendations for environmental improvement, including the identification of investment opportunities for organic WTE; 2. Assessment of organic WTE investment opportunities (e.g. biogas, biomethane) on the island of Fernando de Noronha; 3. Formulation of a project document for the main phase and mobilization of climate finance for the implementation.

projects.name: UNDRR - "Making Cities Resilient 2030" - Implementation of Risks & Resilience Capacities Assessment Tools (QRE & Scorecard)
projects.description:
The Making Cities Resilient 2030 initiative held technical assistance workshops across Brazil to support local governments in applying risks assessment and disaster resilience capacities assessment tools, namely the Quick Risk Estimation tool (QRE) and the Disaster Resilience Scorecard for Cities.

The Scorecard is a tool for disaster resilience planning offered by UNDRR, with the design support of USAID, European Commission, IBM, and AECOM. It provides a set of assessments that allow local governments to assess their disaster resilience, structuring around UNDRR’s Ten Essentials for Making Cities Resilient. It also helps to monitor and review progress and challenges in the implementation of the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction: 2015-2030 and supports the baseline analysis for preparation of the disaster risk reduction and resilience strategies.

The Quick Risk Estimation (QRE) tool serves the purposes of identifying and understanding current and future risks to both human and physical assets. The QRE Tool is not a full scale risk assessment, rather a multi-stakeholder engagement process to establish a common understanding. 

In Brazil, UNDRR technically supported the use of the QRE tool in Abaetetuba (PA), Barcarena (PA), Camaragibe (PE), Jaboatão dos Guararapes (PE), Olinda (PE) and Recife (PE). Whereas the use of the Scorecard was assisted in Porto Alegre (RS), Natal (RN), Santo André (SP), Campinas (SP), Petropolis (RJ), Nova Iguaçu (RJ), Barcarena (PA), Camaragibe (PE), Jaboatão dos Guararapes (PE), Olinda (PE), Recife (PE). All in all, 10 Brazilian cities received the technical support of UNDRR, via the MCR2030 initiative and UNDRR's partners' support (i.e., ICLEI, CEMADEN), to perform risk and resilience capacities assessment at the local level.
